title: Fill a three-day dose tray from a regimen
instruction: Fill the dose tray with one cup per due dose and nothing else. Days 1 to 3 run left to right; the near row is 08:00, the far row 20:00. Blue is first due day 2 08:00, then every 24 h. Red is first due day 1 20:00, then every 48 h.
context: Caregivers and pharmacy technicians fill day-by-time dose trays every week, and a crew's medication for a mission is packed on the ground before flight. WHO names medication errors a leading cause of avoidable harm in health care. Filling a dose tray is bench work done in 1 g, as here. The test is turning a written regimen, a first dose and an interval per drug, into the right cells of a day-by-time grid while leaving the other cells empty. Nothing in the scene marks the answer: there are six cells for four doses and a spare cup of each colour, so filling every cell, one colour everywhere, reading the days right to left or taking every interval as 24 h all score 0. A dose in the wrong slot scores 0, as it would fail a pharmacist's check, while a missed dose costs a quarter. Unlike sorting by type or counting to a stated number, which cells to fill follows from schedule arithmetic.
setup: Station table, in front of the left arm and left of the midline; the right arm is idle at its ready pose. Table coordinates in metres: x forward from the line through the two arm bases, y left from the midline, heights above the table top; the left arm's base is at y = +0.305. All parts are rigid and matte with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic). Fixed, dark grey (sRGB 0.25, 0.25, 0.27): the tray base, a plate 156 x 236 x 3 mm (x, y, z) centred at (0.240, 0.230), spanning x 0.162 to 0.318 and y 0.112 to 0.348. Fixed, light grey (sRGB 0.80, 0.80, 0.80): six cell pads 56 x 56 x 2 mm lying on the base, their tops 5 mm above the table, centred at x = 0.200 (the near row, 08:00) and x = 0.280 (the far row, 20:00) and at y = 0.310 (day 1), 0.230 (day 2) and 0.150 (day 3): 80 mm apart, with 24 mm of dark base between pads and 10 mm round the outside. Day 1 is on the left as seen from behind the arms, which is also the left of the top camera image. The tray carries no labels; the regimen is only in the instruction. Loose: six dose cups, plain closed cylinders 30 mm in diameter and 45 mm tall, 25 g each, rigid plastic, standing on the table, three blue (sRGB 0.20, 0.40, 0.85) and three red (sRGB 0.85, 0.20, 0.20). Left supply column at y = 0.400: blue at x = 0.140, red at 0.220, blue at 0.300. Right supply column at y = 0.060: red at x = 0.140, blue at 0.220, red at 0.300. Cups in a column are 80 mm apart (50 mm of air), every cup stands 37 mm clear of the tray base, and nothing touches at the start. Every cup is within 0.39 m and every cell within 0.33 m of the left arm's base. With both arms at their ready poses the top camera sees every cup and every pad. To build it: cut a 3 mm board to 156 x 236 mm, paint it dark grey and tape it to the table; glue on six 56 mm squares of 2 mm light grey card or plastic at the stated centres; use closed cylinders 30 mm across and 45 mm tall, with no opening at either end, printed hollow (or at reduced infill) to 25 g, three painted blue and three red; tape marks for the six start spots.
scoring: End state only, judged after the arm has released and moved clear, from a top photo and a tape measure; in simulation on the final step. A cup stands in a cell when it is at rest (under 10 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s), upright either way up (axis within 10 degrees of vertical), its lowest point within 4 mm of the pad top and its centre within 20 mm of that cell's centre. The regimen makes four cells due: blue at day 2 08:00 and day 3 08:00, red at day 1 20:00 and day 3 20:00. Day 1 08:00 and day 2 20:00 must stay empty, and one cup of each colour is spare. Gate first: the score is 0 if a cell holds a cup of the wrong colour, if a cup stands in a cell that must stay empty, if two cups stand in one cell, or if a cup at rest has its centre over the tray base without standing in a cell (lying, tilted more than 10 degrees, between cells, more than 20 mm off a cell centre, or on another cup). Otherwise score = correctly filled cells / 4, so 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75 or 1.0. Any cup of a colour may fill any cell due that colour. Cups off the tray (on their marks, elsewhere on the table or off it) and cups still moving count neither way. Success, which ends the trial, is a score of 1.0 held for 1 s. Success also needs every cup whose centre is over the tray to be at rest, so a cup still rolling or sliding across the tray holds it off. The start state scores 0 because no cup is in a cell. Reference outcomes: all six cells filled, 0. One colour in every due cell, 0. Every 24 h for both colours puts red in day 2 20:00, a cell that must stay empty, so 0. Every 48 h for both colours misses day 3 08:00, 0.75. Days read right to left, or the rows swapped, 0. A spare knocked onto the tray, or a cup spilled in its own cell, 0. Values exactly on a limit pass (0.1 mm margin). In simulation every test uses each cup's centre and axis, not its axis-aligned bounds, and the scorer cannot see the gripper, so a cup held motionless over the tray reads as resting there; on the real rig the photo after the arm withdraws decides. The tray and pads are fixed in simulation; on the real rig a trial in which the tray or a pad moves more than 5 mm from its mark scores 0.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. Stand the six cups back on their marks in the two supply columns; the tray and its pads do not move.
fidelity: Approximate: rigid primitives with one shared friction (1.2 static, 1.0 dynamic) and matte colours. The cups are closed 30 x 45 mm cylinders standing in for filled dose cups, and colour stands in for the drug label. The cells are flat pads, not walled compartments, so a cup is in a cell by position. No lids, labels or tablets. Earth gravity on a bench, which is also where dose trays are filled.
